item.title: US P/C Insurers See Fewer Ratings Downgrades in H1 2026 on Improved Performance
item.description: property/casualty insurance segment saw substantially fewer ratings downgrades with more ratings upgrades in the first half of 2026 — mostly related to either poor or improved operating performance, according to AM Best. There were about half as many downgrades in the first half of 2026 — or 3.8% of total rating actions, compared to 6.1% in the same period last year, said the ratings agency in a report titled “ Substantially Fewer Downgrades for US P/C Insurers in First Half of 2026 .” Upgrades increased to 8.2% of total rating actions in the first half of 2026, compared to 5.5% in H1 2025, the report continued. “Over half of downgrades were driven by poor operating performance, as some insurers have struggled to keep losses under control.

item.title: Arity launches customer acquisition platform for insurers
item.description: Arity , the mobility data and analytics company founded by Allstate, has introduced Arity Lead Platform to help insurers manage customer acquisition across lead providers, marketplaces, agency networks and carrier systems. The platform builds on its experience connecting insurers with publishers, marketplaces and other acquisition partners. item.title: Alliant formalizes data center risk advisory offering
item.description: Alliant Insurance Services has formalized an integrated risk advisory offering for developers, owners, investors and contractors involved in hyperscale infrastructure and data center projects. The offering draws on proprietary historical data and experience across hundreds of digital infrastructure projects approaching $1 trillion in project value. The offering brings together specialists in construction, power and energy, environmental risk, cyber, real estate, surety, trade credit, cargo and marine insurance, alongside contract review capabilities.

item.title: Corgi launches data center insurance program
item.description: Corgi has launched a data center insurance program covering construction, operations and computing hardware. The program targets colocation operators, GPU cloud and AI compute hosts, enterprise and edge data centers, and developers. The program combines builders risk and delay in start-up coverage during construction with property and business income coverage once a facility is operational.

item.title: Ripe launches online classic car insurance in the UK

item.title: Commercial Express to withdraw static caravan product
item.description: UK MGA Commercial Express will withdraw its static caravan insurance product effective November 1, 2026, following a strategic review of its portfolio. item.title: Laws to Protect Workers from AI Risks Signed by California Governor
item.description: Gavin Newsom signed laws Wednesday aimed at protecting workers from the threats of artificial intelligence, including potential job losses and workplace surveillance. The laws ban employers from using the technology to predict a worker’s emotional state by using their biometric data, require employers to send written notices to workers if AI is responsible for mass layoffs and ban employers from relying on AI to decide to fire someone. The Democratic governor also signed an executive order to require state agencies to continue to refer to the technology as “artificial intelligence” instead of the term ” super intelligence ” President Donald Trump recently ordered U.S.

item.title: US States Allege Corteva Spinoff a Bid to Evade PFAS Liabilities
item.description: The states allege that the Vylor spinoff transferred one of Corteva’s most profitable businesses to a new company while leaving PFAS liabilities behind, amounting to an effort to defraud creditors pursuing claims against former DuPont entities. Fifteen US states sued agrichemicals company Corteva on Thursday, alleging that the spinoff of its seed and genetics business into Vylor was designed to shield the company’s best assets from tens of billions of dollars in potential liabilities tied to PFAS “forever chemicals” that have polluted the environment. Corteva said in September that the states’ PFAS claims are “speculative and unproven,” adding that Corteva itself never made or sold PFAS products.

item.description: Proposed changes to the federal terrorism insurance backstop could raise the program trigger to $10 million from $5 million and require insurers to absorb more terrorism-related losses, according to new commentary from AM Best. The proposed Terrorism Risk Insurance Program (TRIA) Program Reauthorization Act of 2026 would extend the current Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act (TRIPRA), now set to expire at the end of 2027, through Dec. item.description: Prior to his expanded role, Neary led the former East region for five years, and will continue to report to Matt Stadler, President, Marsh Agency, who commented: “Under Andrew’s leadership, the East region built one of the strongest operating models and cultures in our business, and I have every confidence that he and his team will do the same for our newly combined region, to the benefit of our colleagues and, most importantly, our clients. item.title: Wawanesa launches WSI after acquiring Everest Canada
item.description: WSI will operate as a distinct organisation within the Wawanesa group of companies, and retain its “highly sought-after” expertise, outstanding talent, and underwriting discipline that established Everest Canada as a respected player in the specialty market. The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company (Wawanesa) has launched WSI, which marks the closing of the acquisition of Everest Insurance Company of Canada (Everest Canada), a move which aims to enhance and accelerate its diversification, growth priorities, and commercial capabilities. The parent company explained that despite the name and logo change from Everest Canada to WSI, “the proven business model and trusted relationships that have earned the confidence of organisations across Canada remain in place.” The new brand aims to combine the agility and technical depth of a specialty insurer, complemented by the financial strength, stability, and long-term outlook of Wawanesa.

item.title: Florida Insurance Agent Pleads Guilty in $300,000 Premium Finance Scheme
item.description: A Florida insurance agent faces years in prison after he pleaded guilty to fraudulently arranging more than $300,000 in premium financing for fake companies, then diverting much of the money to his personal use. Daniel Raney, 41, who managed Raney Insurance and Raney Ventures in Pensacola, was arrested in August after the premium finance company, AFCO Direct, became suspicious, according to the arrest affidavit. The associate general counsel with AFCO filed a complaint with the Florida Department of Financial Services in June 2024, after installment payments on the premium finance loan had stopped, an investigator with DFS explained.

item.title: Freeway Insurance partners with National Debt Relief
item.description: Freeway Insurance , part of Confie, has partnered with National Debt Relief to connect customers facing unsecured debt challenges with debt settlement information and resources. The partnership expands Freeway’s services beyond insurance, providing customers with access to resources for addressing credit card balances, medical bills and other unsecured debt. item.title: Allianz names new CEOs for Allianz Partners and Allianz Direct
item.description: Allianz has appointed Philipp Kroetz as CEO of Allianz Partners and Laurent Floquet as CEO of Allianz Direct, effective November 1, 2026, subject to regulatory approval. Kroetz, who has led Allianz Direct since 2022, will succeed Tomas Kunzmann, who joins the Allianz SE Board of Management on January 1, 2027. item.title: Aon launches professional liability risk analyzer for law firms
item.description: Aon has launched its Professional Liability Risk Analyzer, a tool that helps law firms quantify potential losses and assess how different insurance structures would respond. The analyzer combines firm-specific exposure data and historical loss experience with proprietary modeling built on Aon’s 30-year lawyers’ professional liability claims database. The tool is part of Aon’s broader Risk Analyzer suite.

item.title: NA commercial property insurance rates fall the most in a decade, hard market reverses: Willis
item.description: The North America commercial property insurance market has experienced its sharpest decline in rates a decade, according to broker Willis, with wide-spread double-digit price reductions for clients as the soft market ensues and “the multi-year hard market fully reverses.” Abundant capacity is weighing on property insurance and in large and complex accounts softening has been seen across all program types, the Willis (a WTW business) Insurance Marketplace Realities report makes clear. Property rates also continue to soften in the middle-market, where secondary peril exposure and risk discipline are shaping outcomes, Willis explained. The broker reports that rates for large and complex property insurance programs fell by an average of 14.5% in the second quarter of 2026, an acceleration from 8.4% in the prior year, while shared and layered placements fell further with rates down 23.41%, again accelerated from 14.57% in Q2 2025.

item.title: Willis reports sharp fall in North American property insurance rates
item.description: Willis, the insurance brokerage and risk advisory business of WTW, has released its autumn 2026 Insurance Marketplace Realities report, The Specialist View: Navigating Tomorrow’s Risk Landscape for 2027, r eporting that rates for large and complex property risks fell by an average of 14.5% during the second quarter of 2026, compared with an 8.4% reduction during the same period in 2025. Casualty insurance is showing different conditions to the property market, according to Willis. According to Willis, property market conditions have continued to move away from the hard market experienced between 2018 and 2024, with pricing approaching levels last seen in 2019.
